summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for post-procedural monitoring following a scheduled flexible bronchoscopy with balloon dilation and endobronchial biopsy for recurrent tracheal stenosis related to relapsing polychondritis. He tolerated the procedure well with no respiratory compromise. Post-procedural pain was managed with acetaminophen and oxycodone, and his symptoms improved over the hospital stay. He had mild bloody tracheal discharge, which was expected. Laboratory results showed elevated white blood cell count, attributed to inflammation rather than infection. Chest imaging before and after the procedure showed no complications such as pneumothorax. He was discharged home with a short supply of oxycodone, instructions to continue his chronic medications including prednisone and methotrexate, and follow-up appointments scheduled with interventional pulmonology, rheumatology, and infectious disease.
problems: Other specified diseases of upper respiratory tract
